rationale_evidence.anchor: Q6 — extend the model, or map onto it? ... MAP. Tested element by element
rationale_evidence.statement: Ontology/meta-model elements map onto the existing decision model rather than extending it: archetype classification extends DetermineArtifactType (same question, richer vocabulary); KNOWLEDGE != ARTIFACT (I-1) is presupposed by DetermineArtifactLifecycle's deletion litmus; AUTHORITY-SCOPE/CONTAINER boundary maps to DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS/EVIDENCE-STATUS maps to DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE (normative force) maps to DetermineApplicableStandards. Nothing in the ontology requires a new decision; the only extension pressure (FREEZE/RETIRE) is not ontology-driven, but comes from the enacted governance record. Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Ontology scope — per schema file, as parsed ... THE 13% COVERAGE IS A DECLARED BOUNDARY, NOT AN OVERSIGHT
rationale_evidence.statement: Every schema file (knowledge-schema.yaml the metamodel with 16 fields/18 rules; knowledge-types.yaml 31 document types; knowledge-relationships.yaml 11 typed edges + 4 shortcuts, none expressing governs/produces/consumes/observes; statuses.yaml 8 lifecycle states; authorities.yaml 5 trust levels; knowledge-audiences.yaml 9 audiences; bounded-contexts.yaml 12 product contexts) was parsed with the repository's own YAML loader. Finding: the graph's ~13% document coverage is a declared scope (scope.include: docs/knowledge/**/*.md), not an oversight — extending it would amend a declared scope, a governance act, not fix a bug.

rationale_evidence.anchor: knowledge-types.yaml IS a documentation ontology — I checked the temptation to call it a hybrid, and it is not one ... These are documents ABOUT domain objects
rationale_evidence.statement: knowledge-types.yaml is confirmed as a documentation ontology, not a hybrid: types like 'aggregate' or 'event' look like domain objects but their own descriptions are documentary ('aggregate' = a single aggregate's design, invariants, and boundary; 'event' = a domain event's payload/producers/consumers) — these are documents about domain objects, not the domain objects themselves.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in the existing schemas ... KEY COLLISION — mechanical, not aesthetic
rationale_evidence.statement: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in knowledge-types.yaml or bounded-contexts.yaml: (1) key collision, mechanical and decisive — bounded-contexts.yaml already contains a 'governance' key (product-side, code_path app/Contexts/Governance), so adding D-1 'Engineering Governance' would collide with an existing key in a lint-enforced enum; (2) vocabulary insufficiency, strong — the domain model's verbs (governs, produces, consumes, validates, derives, depends on, observes) have no expression in the edge vocabulary (depends_on, derived_from, verified_by), which lacks governs/produces/consumes/observes; (3) subject mismatch, strong — every L-A field is a property of a document (knowledge_id, last_review, code_refs), but 'Engineering Method' has no reviewer, next-review date, or code refs, so it cannot carry a knowledge card. Verdict: D-1..D-7 belong to L-B (which does not yet exist); expressing them as data would require a separate vocabulary file with its own enum namespace, an ARB decision.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The five commissioned deliverables ... L-B ↔ L-A relationship | L-B would OWN and CLASSIFY L-A; L-A would never contain L-B
rationale_evidence.statement: L-B would own and classify L-A, never the reverse: L-A's subject is the document, L-B's subject is the platform — one is the metadata of artifacts, the other the architecture of the thing that produces them. The executable ontology should not change to accommodate L-B; two separately-warranted, ARB-only changes exist: whether scope.include should extend beyond docs/knowledge/** (a declared-scope amendment, not a bug fix), and whether the edge vocabulary needs governs/produces/consumes/observes, answerable only after L-B exists.
